article_candidates.headline: Age-relative-to-level is a credible dollar-surplus signal — but it splits sign against wRC+
article_candidates.hook: The hidden minor-league number that predicts trade earning power isn't a scouting grade. It's how old the player was for his level — and the market is pricing it backwards depending on what you measure.
article_candidates.thesis: receiver_acquired_milb_age_advantage (expected level age minus actual age — positive = young-for-level) clears the V3 credibility threshold on dollar_surplus (beta=+0.041, mass=98.2%, 90% CI [0.008, 0.074]) but flips negative on wrc_delta (beta=-0.032, mass=90.4%) and xfip_delta (beta=-0.017, mass=72%, pitching positive=worse). Young-for-level prospects produce dollar surplus through arriving on cost-controlled contracts — but they regress on rate-stat production once acquired. This is a salary-market efficiency, not a production efficiency. Old-for-level acquisitions (age_adv <= -3) post mean WAR delta of -0.09 in raw splits while on-level acquisitions average +0.36 — confirming the asymmetry: young-for-level wins on cheap surplus, on-level wins on WAR.

evidence.stat_summary: dollar_surplus: beta=+0.041, mass=98.2%, credible (V3, train_n=3578, test_n=1730). wrc_delta: beta=-0.032, mass=90.4% directional. Stratified: age_adv<=-3 (old-for-level) mean WAR delta y+1 = -0.09 (n=440); -3<age_adv<=-1 = +0.18 (n=314); on-level = +0.36 (n=314); old = +0.28 (n=132).

article_candidates.actionable_takeaway: When acquiring prospects, prioritize age-for-level over scouting grade depth: the dollar-surplus signal is the salary side, not the production side. Don't overpay for young-for-level rate-stat production — it regresses. Do bid hard on cost-controlled service-time delivery from the same cohort.

article_candidates.headline: FanGraphs FV grades are noise in trade outcomes — MiLB hit quality is the real signal
article_candidates.hook: Eight prospect-grade features were tested against five trade outcomes. The famous one — FanGraphs Future Value — never clears 70% directional mass. The unfamiliar one — a level-adjusted OPS proxy from MiLB box scores — clears 88% directional mass on four separate outcomes.
article_candidates.thesis: Across V3 backtests on war_delta, dollar_surplus, xwoba_delta, wrc_delta, and xfip_delta, receiver_acquired_avg_fv and receiver_acquired_max_fv never exceed 84% directional mass and never have 90% CIs that exclude zero. receiver_acquired_milb_hit_quality (level-adjusted OPS times PA weight) posts directional mass >= 88% on all four hitting-relevant outcomes (war_delta 91.3%, xwoba_delta 89.8%, xfip_delta 88.5%, dollar_surplus 80.9%) with consistent positive sign. Stratified Q1 vs Q3 hit_quality buckets show +0.07 vs +0.44 WAR delta — a 6x difference. The trade-evaluator's FV grade is doing less predictive work than aggregated MiLB box-score performance, suggesting the market over-prices scouting consensus relative to underlying minor-league rate stats.

evidence.stat_summary: hit_quality directional mass: war 91.3%, xwoba 89.8%, xfip 88.5%, wrc 78%. FV: max 60.8% (war), 66.3% (dollar), 54% (xwoba). Stratified hit_quality quartiles: Q1=+0.07, Q2=+0.29, Q3=+0.44, Q4=+0.31 mean WAR delta y+1. Note: avg_fv/max_fv sample is only n=22 trades with non-zero values — most acquired-player sets don't contain ranked prospects.

article_candidates.actionable_takeaway: Don't valuate a prospect deal on consensus FV grade alone. Pull the trailing-season MiLB slash line, weight by level, and look for the Q3 sweet spot — the players consistently above average without elite tags. Reserve top-FV chips for return on dollar value, not WAR.

article_candidates.headline: The pitching prospect signal is non-monotonic — Q2 minor-league arms outperform Q4 elites in trade outcomes
article_candidates.hook: Better minor-league ERA does not produce better post-trade WAR in a straight line. The second-best MiLB pitchers in trade returns generate twice the surplus of the very best.
article_candidates.thesis: Splitting trades by receiver_acquired_milb_pitch_quality quartile reveals a non-monotonic pattern: Q1=+0.14, Q2=+0.42, Q3=+0.21, Q4=+0.21 mean WAR delta y+1. The Q2 mean is double Q4 with equal sample size (n=101 per bucket). In the V3 multivariate model, pitch_quality directional mass is weak across all outcomes (max 68% on dollar_surplus). This is a classic flag-tier rather than tape-tier finding — the elite-MiLB-arsenal prospects are priced like elite arms, the second-tier are priced like backend depth, and the realized outcomes invert that pricing. Suggests acquiring teams systematically overpay for top-quartile minor-league pitching performance and underpay for solid-but-unspectacular MiLB pitchers in deal packages.

evidence.stat_summary: Quartile means of WAR delta y+1 (n=101 per bucket): Q1=+0.14, Q2=+0.42, Q3=+0.21, Q4=+0.21. V3 multivariate directional mass: war 56.5%, dollar 68.3%, xwoba 61.4%, xfip 60.1%. Univariate effect doesn't survive multivariate controls cleanly.

article_candidates.actionable_takeaway: Don't lead deal packages with the top MiLB pitching prospects when targeting WAR. Demand the Q2 throw-ins; they post the highest mean realized WAR delta in this sample. Pricing inefficiency is testable: re-run with park-adjusted xERA in MiLB once available.

dead_ends_explored.angle: FanGraphs The Board FV vs trade outcomes
dead_ends_explored.reason: Only 22 trades in the entire 2010-2024 backtester have any acquired player with a non-zero FV grade (most ranked prospects aren't traded). FV consensus / divergence features all sit at ~50% directional mass — pure noise. The Board ingest is well-formed (498 player-years) but the join with trade events is too sparse for credible inference.

dead_ends_explored.angle: MiLB TJBat (TJStats batting metric) on trade outcomes
dead_ends_explored.reason: Only 5 rows in trade_acquired_milb_tjbat have non-null values. Coefficients are exactly symmetric around zero — the prior is just being recovered. Wait for TJStats backfill before re-running.

dead_ends_explored.angle: Player-alumni effects (traded back to original org)
dead_ends_explored.reason: No player-level alumni network feature exists. alumni_network.py is hand-coded for front-office (Luhnow / Sig HOU pioneer window) and contains zero player records. Would require new feature engineering from trade_player_unified joined to draft_picks — not in current V3 feature set.

dead_ends_explored.angle: Origin-org dev cluster as proxy for prospect inflation by org
dead_ends_explored.reason: receiver_acquired_from_dev_cluster_score has 56% directional mass on war_delta — null. The feature exists but cluster assignments don't differentiate post-trade outcomes credibly. Would need higher-resolution org features (per-position-group dev signature).
